faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Salary Expectations

When you’re negotiating a job offer or planning your finances, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. Your **salary expectations** should be based on accurate calculations that account for the hours you work, the type of employment, and the legal minimums set by Australian workplace laws.

This guide explains the conversion formula, the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, how casual loading works, and what you can expect for tax and superannuation.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The standard way to estimate your annual gross salary is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the ordinary hours used by the Fair Work Commission), the formula becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year

This is your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. It assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

If you are paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. At the National Minimum Wage, a fortnight would be $2,009.80.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the **National Minimum Wage** each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week. This is the minimum an employer can pay an adult employee who is not covered by an award or enterprise agreement.

However, most employees in Australia are covered by a **modern award** that applies to their industry or occupation. Awards often set higher minimum pay rates, along with penalty rates, allowances, and overtime rules. To find the correct rate for your job, check the pay guides published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Your salary expectations should reflect the award rate that applies to your classification, not the National Minimum Wage, unless you are award/agreement-free.

### Casual Loading

If you are a **casual employee**, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The Fair Work Commission sets this at 25% for award/agreement-free employees. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements like annual leave, sick leave, and public holiday pay.

When using our [timesheet](/blog), you can check the casual loading box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Superannuation

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an employee earning $52,254.80, the super contribution would be $6,270.58 (12% of $52,254.80). Super does not reduce your take-home pay; it is an extra payment from your employer.

### Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners.

For an annual salary of $52,254.80, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $8,000–$9,000, depending on your circumstances. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more precise estimate.

### Putting It All Together

Your salary expectations should be based on the correct minimum rate for your job, whether that is the National Minimum Wage or an award rate. Remember:

- Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 for a standard full-time year.
- Check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog).
- Add casual loading if applicable.
- Super is paid on top at 12%.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay.

For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
